items.title: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal
items.excerpt: The European Commission published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting AI Act implementation in the Official Journal of the EU, a milestone ahead of the application of high-risk AI system requirements; further harmonised standards are expected to follow.
items.note: PRIMARY document (EU). Compliance with a harmonised standard gives presumption of conformity under the AI Act.

items.title: AI sovereignty: preserving UK agency in an AI-enabled world
items.excerpt: A published advisory letter to the UK Minister for AI sets out how the UK can build the capability to make strategic choices about current and future AI technology, framed as preserving national agency.
items.note: PRIMARY document (UK government publication). Generic gov.uk og:image.

items.title: The EU AI Act Mandates AI Incident Reporting—If We're Lucky
items.excerpt: Hannes Bastians and Maarten Herbosch argue OpenAI's disclosure of the July Hugging Face incident to the EU AI Office shows the AI Act's serious-incident duty can work, but its definitions leave gaps for frontier models acting as attackers or not placed on the EU market.
items.note: Analysis (not a decision). Page shows Oct 19 1:00 PM ET; Google News stamp 17:04Z. Related to 10-15 published AI Office info requests - analysis only.

items.title: Is Europe Ready for Advanced AI? The Growing Debate Over Liability
items.excerpt: Ramsha Jahangir talks with the Future of Life Institute's Risto Uuk and MEP Brando Benifei about Europe's AI policy debate and renewed calls for AI liability rules.

items.title: OpenAI Faces Lawsuits, Subpoenas and EU Scrutiny in a Single Week
items.excerpt: Tech Policy Press's weekly roundup of the legal and regulatory pressure on OpenAI, from state lawsuits and subpoenas to EU AI Office scrutiny.
items.note: Weekly roundup; largely recaps already-published 10-15 items (8-state suit, AI Office requests). Low priority.

items.title: Thought for the week: Preparing for AI incidents
items.excerpt: IAPP argues organizations with established crisis and cyber response plans should update their playbooks to handle AI incidents as incident-reporting regimes take shape.

items.title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
items.excerpt: The Verge reports Democratic candidates are testing tougher AI regulation as a midterm message, though the issue remains open for either party to claim.
items.note: Public-opinion/campaign framing; keep non-partisan, attribute claims.

items.title: JB Pritzker on the good and bad of AI
items.excerpt: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker discusses state AI laws, privacy, data centers and Congress's role, comparing AI's risks to nuclear proliferation.

items.title: The AI attack-ad nightmare is coming true
items.excerpt: An Axios analysis found numerous midterm political ads partly or fully made with generative AI, often undisclosed, including Senate Leadership Fund deepfake ads of Sen. Jon Ossoff; four states prohibit certain AI deepfake ads, 27 require disclosure, and no federal law specifically regulates them.
items.note: DEDUP RISK: cites Wesleyan $137M figure published 10-19; new element is Axios's own ad analysis + state-law tally. axios.com 403s curl/WebFetch; time read via r.jina.ai Published Time.

items.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
items.excerpt: Court filings in Character.AI's Chapter 11 case show Disney required the deal be consummated through bankruptcy, seeking a perpetual license via a '363 free and clear' order while Character.AI retains liability for chatbot child-safety lawsuits.
items.note: Liability angle via bankruptcy filings. Same WIRED story also at wired.com/story/disney-asked-characterai-to-go-bankrupt-for-a-get-out-of-lawsuits-card/ (10-19T09:00Z) - one story. Prior published: Verge NY AG Character.AI bankruptcy; 40 AGs (10-15).

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog "employee-like" access
items.excerpt: Anthropic has granted an outside AI watchdog employee-like access to its systems, and the watchdog can publish findings without Anthropic's approval.
items.note: Voluntary governance/third-party oversight; not a government action.

items.title: Microsoft abandons UK AI supercomputer as grid struggles to keep up
items.excerpt: Microsoft has walked away from its flagship Essex AI supercomputer project as UK power-connection delays threaten to push the nation's AI compute ambitions into the 2030s.
items.note: Sovereign compute / grid policy angle; pairs with UK AI sovereignty letter.

items.title: Will developing nations be able to handle millions of AI agents?
items.excerpt: Rest of World examines whether AI agents from Meta, OpenAI and others can navigate the infrastructure, regulatory and cultural complexities of developing nations.

items.title: Daedalus: Greece unveils new supercomputer as it eyes role in Europe's AI race
items.excerpt: Greece inaugurated Daedalus, a €58.9 million, 85.69-petaflop supercomputer in Lavrio ranked 31st worldwide, letting researchers and businesses train AI models on data kept within the country.
items.note: Sovereign AI compute. curl gets 406; date/image via WebFetch (image inferred from article body).

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang warns Germany is falling behind in AI race
items.excerpt: Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Nvidia's Jensen Huang are set to unveil a joint AI pact to speed AI integration across German industry, as Huang warns Germany is falling behind.
items.note: Government-industry AI pact (formal pact text not yet seen).

items.title: Cyberattack on French supermarkets tells us more about food security than AI safety
items.excerpt: Experts know little about the hackers who remotely raised temperatures in French supermarket refrigerators, POLITICO reports, arguing the incident says more about critical-infrastructure security than AI safety.
items.note: Weak AI hook (AI-safety framing debunk) - may fail 'delete AI' test.

items.title: Taiwan targets illicit AI server exports to China with five-year prison terms
items.excerpt: Taiwan is moving to criminalize unauthorized exports of AI servers and chips to China with up to five years in prison, following a US tariff deal and a Super Micro smuggling raid, which could make it easier to charge AI chip smugglers.
items.note: OFF-LIST exception (tomshardware.com): no allowed outlet covered this geopolitics action in-window. Status (proposal vs. cabinet approval) unconfirmed - verify against Executive Yuan/MOEA text.
